analysis:
Examined workflow metadata, full BASE/HEAD, patch, changelog and build-documentation changes against the canonical definition index and supplied TB-002/TB-009 detail. In .github/workflows/darkbloom-watchdog.yml:112-138,194-198, JSON aggregation moves from argv to files/stdin, removing an argument-size availability failure. Files remain within the existing private mktemp directory, are used sequentially and cleaned on exit; pagination and HTTP response limits are unchanged. No new executable interpretation of API data or token disclosure was identified.
At head:238-242, cancellation eligibility no longer considers recent completions or the attempt's last completion: an old queued shard can trigger rescue despite sibling work still running. This is explicitly documented in changelog.d/darkbloom-watchdog-listing-size.md:4-5 and docs/developer/build.md:439-449. Existing write permissions, attempt check, watchdog-marker coordination, rescue limits and cancel/rerun mechanisms remain unchanged (head:248-300). No demonstrated provider authorization, attestation, encryption, cache, billing or privileged-helper regression follows from this local change; T-043 concerns the provider's separate crash-recovery watchdog, not this GitHub workflow.
Integration should verify that jobs affected by the expanded whole-run cancellation tolerate interruption/reexecution, particularly any artifact publication or qualification work involving A-011/A-017, and that the route/fallback contract actually applies on rerun. Those callers and route implementation are not supplied; their failure cannot be assumed and is not reported as a vulnerability. The external template's claimed provenance was not independently verified.
